subject: Production latency spike tied to client adapter backpressure / streaming parse failure
messages:
From: Jane Lewis <jane.lewis@cartwheel.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-08-09T09:12:34-07:00
Subject: Urgent: sudden spike in 5xx & tail latency after SDK update

Karthik —

We started seeing a sharp rise in 5xx errors and per-request tail latency at ~09:05 PDT following our auto-deploy of the Cartwheel client integration that bundles Redwood client SDK v2.3.1. Error rate jumped from ~0.4% to ~7% and overall throughput for the checkout path dropped by ~38%. Traces attached (cartwheel_request_traces_20270809.zip).

Symptoms:
- 502 / 504 in the logs, often preceded by long stalls (~2–6s) before the request eventually fails.
- Retries from our middleware layer spike, which amplifies load and causes cascading failures.
- We observed repeated "missing pseudo-header" entries in a subset of the traces.

We rolled back to SDK v2.2.8 on a handful of hosts which helped reduce the rate, but we need full remediation. This outage is impacting checkout success rate and we are escalating internally to our CIO. We need a hot path: what mitigation can Redwood apply now? Can you route our traffic to an older parser or provide a short-term configuration to disable aggressive client-side retry behavior?

Please treat as P1 — we are available to jump on a call.

Thanks,
Jane Lewis
Sr. Engineering Manager, Platform
Cartwheel Retail

Attachments: cartwheel_request_traces_20270809.zip
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Lewis <jane.lewis@cartwheel.com>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-08-09T09:27:10-07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: sudden spike in 5xx & tail latency after SDK update

Jane — thanks for the quick heads-up and logs. Really sorry you hit this. I'm opening an incident and pulling in SRE + client SDK immediately.

Immediate actions we are taking (now):
- SRE (Dev Patel) is triaging traces and will look for patterns in connection lifecycles / resets.
- Engineering (Dylan) is checking our v2.3.1 release notes and reproducing with your traces.
- CS (Marissa) will coordinate a short mitigation runbook and customer comms.

Short-term mitigations we can enact from our side:
- Temporarily pin your tenant to the older streaming parser pool (will cutover within 10–15 minutes if you approve) — this is a low-risk rollback of routing.
- Disable server-side aggressive retry amplification for your API key until the root-cause is fixed.

Ask from you: if you can provide a small pcap or exact curl/synthetic that reproduces the problem (we see a pattern but need definitive repro to validate fix). If you can also confirm which subset of hosts were rolled back to 2.2.8, that helps.

I'm marking this P1. We'll update every 30 minutes or on any material change.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Production Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, jane.lewis@cartwheel.com
Date: 2027-08-09T10:05:44-07:00
Subject: Initial triage: malformed trailers and backpressure pattern observed

Team — quick triage notes after ingesting Jane's traces and sampling traffic from Cartwheel's key:

What we see:
- A subset (~12%) of streams show unexpected pseudo-header sequences in the application-level stream frames. Example from trace: 
  ":status=200
  content-length=128
  \"x-rt-trailer\"=\"
  followed by an immediate stream close with no END_STREAM flag observed on the server side.
- Our streaming parser attempts to reassemble headers across small interleaved frames; when it encounters the malformed trailer it treats it as a header block and triggers early header validations that result in connection aborts.
- The client integration's retry policy (on the Cartwheel side) retries aggressively after connection aborts which creates transient overload — this is likely the throughput drop + higher error surface.

Evidence attached: sre_initial_trace.txt (extracted snippets). I also pulled histograms showing increased tail latency correlating to periods where interleaved small writes occur.

Next steps I recommend now:
1) Switch Cartwheel to the parser-compat pool (we can toggle this per-key).
2) Request Cartwheel to throttle client-side fast retries for 30 minutes while we validate.
3) SDK team to produce a quick patch to add header/trailer sanity checks and a staging build we can smoke-test against the problematic traces.

If we can get a pcap or reproduction harness that does 3–4 concurrent small writes that interleave headers and payload, the SDK team can reproduce locally.

-Dev
Dev Patel
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: sre_initial_trace.txt
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: dev_patel@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, jane.lewis@cartwheel.com
Date: 2027-08-09T13:48:10-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial triage: malformed trailers and backpressure pattern observed

Thanks Dev — we reproduced the failure pattern locally within 90 minutes using the traces Jane provided. Root cause summary and plan:

Root cause (summary):
- A race condition in our HTTP/2 pseudo-header reassembly path in the v2.3.x client adapter causes trailer-like bytes from interleaved small payload frames to be consumed as header continuation. That leads to a parser state that fails header validation and closes the stream without an END_STREAM.
- Downstream behavior: client libraries see a connection abort and trigger configured retry policies. The resulting retry amplification leads to throughput collapse and tail latency spikes observed by Cartwheel.

Fix and mitigations:
- Hotfix: preparing 2.3.2 release that adds conservative header/trailer sanity checks, a state-machine guard against treating small interleaved writes as header continuations, and an opt-in backpressure knob for older clients. Patch diff attached (sdk_hotfix_2.3.2.patch.diff).
- Deployment plan: immediate canary to a subset of parser nodes (10% traffic) in ~1 hour, monitor error rate & p99 latency for 30 minutes, then roll to 100% if green.
- Workaround we recommend now: 1) toggle Cartwheel to parser-compat pool (Karthik can make the switch), or 2) have Cartwheel temporarily cap retries to 1 and add exponential jitter.

Timeline:
- 13:50 PDT: publish 2.3.2 canary build and deploy to parser-canary nodes.
- 14:30 PDT: monitor and validate against Cartwheel traces.
- 15:15 PDT: roll to full fleet if metrics are stable.

I'll coordinate with Marissa for customer comms. Karthik/Dev — please let me know when you flip the parser-compat pool and if Cartwheel is able to throttle retries. I'll also prepare a short post-mortem draft after the patch.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Senior Software Engineer, Client SDKs
Redwood Inference
